reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its primary purpose is to announce a $75 Ulta or Sephora gift-card giveaway and accompanying Q&A. Participation involves subscribing and leaving a question in the comments, with sharing encouraged, rather than providing payment, investment, credentials, or other transaction requirements. Although the title and description differ about whether the giveaway is closed, the described material does not establish a deceptive mechanism.

citations.quote: I will be giving away a gift card and I'm gonna to give you the choice to pick either Ulta or Sephora
I'll be doing $75 so if you want to join this contest you just have to be subscribed and then leave a comment below.
I'm gonna have this contest go for about a month so starting, I think December 1st is when I'm gonna end the contest and then I'll answer all of your questions and announce the winner
ULTA/SEPHORA $75 GIFT CARD GIVEAWAY!!(CLOSED)

opening.argument: The promised $75 reward is directly conditioned on audience actions: viewers must subscribe and comment, while the description also urges them to share. That makes this more than a passive announcement; it is a solicitation that acquires engagement by attaching a valuable gift card to low-effort participation. The video gives no independently verifiable fulfillment process, selection method, or proof that the promised reward will be delivered, so the attractive promise-action pairing is the central concern.

citations.quote: I'll be doing $75 so if you want to join this contest you just have to be subscribed and then leave a comment below.
So be sure to enter, share with all your friends and family, and good luck!!
I will be giving away a $75 gift card to either Ulta or Sephora, it will be the winner's choice.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of a payment request does not resolve the concern: the proposed exchange is a valuable gift card for subscriptions, comments, and expanded reach. Calling those actions free entry simply restates the solicitation. The claimed month-long period and winner announcement describe an assertion of future delivery, not evidence that delivery is genuine.

citations.quote: if you want to join this contest you just have to be subscribed and then leave a comment below.
then I'll answer all of your questions and announce the winner

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited conditions show ordinary audience participation, not a scam mechanism. Viewers are asked only to subscribe and comment, with no payment, credentials, purchase, or external claim process shown. The criticism that fulfillment details are not independently verified is an argument from omission; it does not show that the giveaway is deceptive.

citations.quote: you just have to be subscribed and then leave a comment below.
I will be giving away a gift card

opening.argument: Several risk signals reinforce one another: the reward is a relatively specific $75 gift card, participation is presented as easy, sharing is encouraged, and the contest has a defined closing date. The title even marks the giveaway as “CLOSED,” while the description describes a future December 1 closing, creating uncertainty about whether viewers are seeing an active opportunity or a completed one. A valuable, low-barrier reward combined with time pressure and inconsistent status is reasonably suspicious.

citations.quote: I will be giving away a $75 gift card to either Ulta or Sephora, it will be the winner's choice.
on December 1st I will be closing it and pick a winner
ULTA/SEPHORA $75 GIFT CARD GIVEAWAY!!(CLOSED)
So be sure to enter, share with all your friends and family, and good luck!!

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats each signal in isolation. It does not explain why the title says “CLOSED” while the description presents a future closing date, or why viewers should trust a valuable reward promoted through sharing. Those unresolved inconsistencies weaken the claim that this is merely a routine promotion.

citations.quote: ULTA/SEPHORA $75 GIFT CARD GIVEAWAY!!(CLOSED)
on December 1st I will be closing it and pick a winner

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The evidence supports a normal contest timeline, not deceptive urgency: the description says the contest will run for about a month and identifies December 1 as the intended closing date. The title's “CLOSED” notation can reflect the video's status rather than a demand for immediate action. Nothing establishes a false reward, an external payment flow, or a fraudulent claim process.

citations.quote: This contest will go for about a month, on December 1st I will be closing it and pick a winner
ULTA/SEPHORA $75 GIFT CARD GIVEAWAY!!(CLOSED)

opening.argument: The apparent Q&A is not neutral community interaction; it is used as the entry mechanism for a subscriber-growth campaign. The speaker asks viewers to subscribe, submit personal questions, and help reach a stated subscriber goal, while the gift card supplies the incentive to participate. The giveaway therefore functions as promotional acquisition: it steers viewers toward engagement and channel growth under the appealing cover of a personal contest.

citations.quote: my goal is to hit three thousand by the end of the year
I just need you guys to help me get there
All you have to do is be subscribed, and comment below and question you may have for me!
ask me anything, and i will answer all of your questions

rebuttal.rebuttal: Describing the activity as a Q&A does not change what viewers are being induced to do. The speaker explicitly connects the contest to subscribing and asks for questions, while separately acknowledging a goal of reaching 3,000 subscribers. That is promotional steering, not merely an informational discussion.

citations.quote: my goal is to hit three thousand by the end of the year
if you want to join this contest you just have to be subscribed and then leave a comment below.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Audience growth is compatible with an ordinary creator giveaway and does not by itself establish fraud. The primary offer remains a contest for a $75 Ulta or Sephora gift card, and the entry requirements are subscription and commenting. The cited subscriber goal shows promotion, but not deception, payment extraction, or a false fulfillment mechanism.
